Subject: QBR prep: capacity prioritization & unit-econ tradeoffs

Team — attaching the QBR pre-read (qbr_capacity_brief_v2.pdf) and the initial slot allocation spreadsheet. High-level framing and asks below. Please review today so I can lock the deck for Friday's leadership rehearsal.

Why this matters (quick): we have a tight runway on GPU hours as Q3 demand grows. Without tighter prioritization we risk SLA pressure on Dedicated customers and material unit-cost drift for hosted API. QBR needs a clear decision on the following 3 levers: reserve buffer for burst capacity, experiment prioritization (batching vs cache vs quantization), and short-term slot allocation per tier.

Headline numbers (current vs proposed):
- Current monthly GPU spend (est): $1,180,000 / month (on-demand + reserved blended)
- Average GPU utilization (30d): 64%
- Target utilization (operational): 75% (within 6 weeks post-experiments)
- Baseline token cost per 1k (hosted): $0.27; projected with batching/caching: $0.22 (-18% token cost)
- Projected savings from 8-week caching rollout (conservative): $80k/mo

Proposal summary:
1) Short-term reserve: 20% capacity buffer for peak hours (rather than 30% previously suggested).
2) Prioritize two experiments in parallel (2-week sprints):
   a) Aggressive batching policy for interactive endpoints (reduce per-token compute by ~12-20% without latency SLO regressions)
   b) Prefix/KV prefetch caching for customer corridors (expected 5-10% additional savings)
3) Defer broad quantization migration for non-critical models until after QBR (we target a pilot for a single model family).

Asks (today):
- Leadership: confirm buffer percentage (20% vs 30%) and approve the two experiment tracks.
- Product/Infra: markus, karthik — confirm feasibility & expected lead times for experiments; update slot-proposal.xlsx with per-customer impact.
- Finance: OLGA — quick sanity check on modeled savings vs spend-impact.

Meeting ask: final decision checkpoint at 4pm PT today (I will circulate an updated slide if we converge).

Attachments: qbr_capacity_brief_v2.pdf, slot-proposal.xlsx

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan
Head of Infrastructure Operations
Redwood Inference

Tessa — quick notes after a run with the infra team and a pass at the spreadsheet (attached: slot-proposal.xlsx, "markus-annotated"). High level: I agree we need a buffer, but 20% is a better tradeoff than 30% given expected utilization gains from batching. Specifics below.

Benchmarks & asks:
- Measured throughput (p50 latency targets preserved) when increasing batch-size window from 20ms->50ms: token-throughput +14% with median latency increase +60ms (still within interactive SLO for tier-2).
- Estimated per-GPU token cost: $0.035/token-hr baseline; with batching + caching combined we model $0.028 (-20%).
- Proposed short-term slot allocation (weekly cadence):
   * Hosted public: 46% (down from 52%)
   * Dedicated: 38% (steady)
   * Burst buffer pool: 16% (this maps to the 20% daily buffer target after accounting for preemptible availability)

Recommendation: Approve 20% buffer and run the two experiments in parallel with a stoplight: green = safe to widen batching window; amber = revert for top 5 customers; red = halt and rollback. I'll add a simple fallback policy to the orchestration config.

Attaching: slot-proposal.xlsx (annotated), short-run benchmarks (excerpt in spreadsheet).

Thanks for the concise framing, Tessa and Markus. Leadership position: we cannot accept material SLA regressions for current customers. That said, the runway risk is real and we need to show near-term action in the QBR. My decisions: 

1) Approve 20% buffer (operationalization note: make it dynamic by region; set a 14-day review).
2) Approve both experiments (batching + caching) for an initial 2-week sprint. Scope: restrict aggressive batching to tier-2 endpoints and non-contract critical customers; caching pilot for corridor traffic only.
3) Finance to model upside scenarios for incremental savings and the downside risk if experiments hit latency regressions. Olga, please produce a 3-scenario P&L before Friday (best/most-likely/worst).

Action items I am assigning now: 
- Tessa: update slides with the buffer decision and two experiments (due EOD).
- Markus: implement the stoplight fallback and add per-customer opt-out list.
- Karthik: prioritize kernel/inference changes for batching and provide ETA on rollout to dedicated pools.

We will keep quantization migration out of the QBR headlines — mention as a pilot next quarter.

Lauren
